notes: §1985:XVI.3.2.3 SR1: 'The segment-number must be an integer ranging in value from 0 through 99.' VisitSectionDefinition calls ScreenSegmentNumber(0, 99), which runs at COBOL-85 (Segmentation.MeaningKept) and reports COBOL6819 for any value above 99 (ValueOf maps more than two significant digits to int.MaxValue); the grammar's integerLiteral already refuses a sign, a decimal point and a name, and a declarative section is held to the tighter SR3 bound by VisitDeclarativeSection. Probes at 85: (f) 0 and 99 run, 100, 0100 and a 23-digit number are COBOL6819 (the last also COBOL2427); (b) -5 and 5.0 refused by the grammar; (c) a number at --std 2002 is COBOL0902. A three-digit spelling with a leading zero (050) passes as 50, which is the value SR1 asks about; its spelling is the word-form defect recorded on 1985-FMT-XVI.3.2.2. The witness's SECTION 100 is COBOL6819.

next.reason: 1985: "The segment-number must be an integer ranging in value from 0 through 99."; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds segmentation or segment-numbers; the Segmentation module is not carried.". No 2023 clause holds the Segmentation feature. The wording candidates cover only level-numbers, THRU and integer operands, so the segment-number range rule is dropped with the module.
